faqLeft.q: What engine does the Mercedes Citan 109 CDI use?
faqLeft.a: It depends on the year. From 2012 to 2021 (W415 generation), the Citan 109 CDI used the K9K 1.5-litre diesel. From 2021 onwards (W420), it uses OM607 or OM608 1.5-litre diesels — different units. Send us your registration and we'll confirm which one your van has.

faqLeft.q: How much does a Mercedes Citan 109 CDI engine rebuild cost?
faqLeft.a: Rebuilds start from £2,200, across all three engine codes. Exact price depends on condition and parts required — submit your reg for a fixed-price quote.

faqLeft.q: Which engine code is fitted to my Citan 109 CDI?
faqLeft.a: Enter your registration on this page and we'll confirm whether you have the K9K, OM607 or OM608 before you're quoted anything.

faqLeft.q: Do you rebuild K9K Citan 109 CDI engines?
faqLeft.a: Yes. We replace injectors, EGR components and gaskets as standard on every K9K rebuild, along with timing chain components where worn.

faqLeft.q: Do you rebuild OM607 Citan 109 CDI engines?
faqLeft.a: Yes. The OM607 is a newer engine and we service it to the same standard as our other Citan rebuilds.

faqRight.q: Do you rebuild OM608 Citan 109 CDI engines?
faqRight.a: Yes. The OM608 is a newer engine and we service it to the same standard as our other Citan rebuilds.

faqRight.q: Do you supply used Citan 109 CDI engines?
faqRight.a: Yes, in some cases a matched low-mileage used engine is the right option. Our team will advise honestly once we've matched your registration and understood your situation.

faqRight.q: Can you recover my Citan 109 CDI if the engine has failed?
faqRight.a: Yes — nationwide recovery is available from £70, and most vehicles are collected within a few hours of booking.

faqRight.q: How long does a Citan 109 CDI engine rebuild take?
faqRight.a: Most rebuilds are completed within 3-5 working days from the time your van arrives at our workshop.

faqRight.q: Is rebuilding better than fitting a used engine?
faqRight.a: For most Citan 109 CDI owners, yes. A rebuild removes the compatibility risk that comes with an unknown used unit's history, and comes with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty — often longer and more comprehensive than what a used engine supplier offers.
